newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thailand to buy Natuna gas, invest in project.
newsitem.headline: Thailand to buy Natuna gas, invest in project.

text.p: Thailand agreed in principle to buy natural gas from Indonesia's huge Natuna Project and to acquire an 11-15 percent stake in the project, Industry Minister Korn Dabbaransi said on Wednesday.

Korn told reporters that Thailand would buy the gas from the field from 2005, taking 500 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd) in the first two years and later increasing its volume to one billion cubic feet per day (Bcfd).

The minister talked to reporters after meeting Indonesian Minister of State for Research and Technology Jusuf Habibie and executives from Exxon Corp and Mobil Corp. Exxon owns a 50 percent stake in the project,
He said the gas price remains to be further negotiated but Thailand had made it clear that it would buy at platform prices.

The Natuna find in the South China Sea is one of the largest gasfields in the world, containing an estimated 222 trillion cubic feet (TCF) of gas, of which 46 TCF are thought to be commerically recoverable. The cost of the development, which Indonesia hopes will replace ageing gasfields in Sumatra, has been estimated at US$40 billion.
